name: Driveway Resurfacing vs Replacement: Which Is Better?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between driveway resurfacing and driveway replacement?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between driveway resurfacing and driveway replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resurfacing is a good option when the driveway surface is worn, stained, or lightly cracked but the base underneath is still stable. The contractor applies a new layer or finish over the existing surface to improve appearance and sometimes extend service life. Replacement is a deeper fix: the old driveway is removed, the subgrade and base are rebuilt if needed, and a new surface is installed. That process costs more and takes longer, but it addresses structural problems that resurfacing cannot solve. In Los Angeles County, replacement is often the better choice if the driveway has significant settlement, recurring cracking, poor drainage, or utility conflicts. Homeowners should ask the contractor to explain what condition the base is in, because a smooth new surface on a weak foundation will not last. The right choice depends on whether the issue is cosmetic or structural, and a proper site inspection should make that clear.
acceptedAnswer.description: Resurfacing adds a new top layer over an existing driveway, while replacement removes the old driveway and rebuilds it from the base up. Resurfacing is cheaper and faster, but it only works when the underlying structure is still sound. Replacement is better when the base has failed, the driveway is uneven, or drainage is poor.
